t: A federal republic of twenty-six cantons, created by Napoleon in 1803 and turned into a federal state by the constitution of 1848.
Its permanent neutrality, recognised in 1815, kept it out of every European war since and made Geneva a centre of diplomacy.
Referendums and popular initiatives give its citizens an unusually direct say in law-making at federal and cantonal level.
dyk: Swiss men voted on whether women should have the federal vote: they refused in 1959 and agreed only in 1971, and Appenzell Innerrhoden had to be ordered by the Federal Supreme Court to admit women in 1990.
ev: Napoleon's Act of Mediation creates a confederation of nineteen cantons
The great powers recognise Switzerland's perpetual neutrality
Federal troops under General Dufour win the Sonderbund War
The Federal Constitution creates a federal state with Bern as federal city
The International Committee of the Red Cross is founded in Geneva
Constitutional revision introduces the optional referendum on federal laws
Women gain the right to vote in federal elections
Switzerland joins the United Nations after a popular vote

f.capital: Rotating directorial cantons (1803–1848); Bern (federal city from 1848)
